definition: Multi-document summarization is an automatic procedure aimed at extraction of information from multiple texts written about the same topic.
details: The resulting summary report allows individual users, such as professional information consumers, to quickly familiarize themselves with information contained in a large cluster of documents. In such a way, multi-document summarization systems are complementing the news aggregators performing the next step down the road of coping with information overload.

explainer.lead: Multi-document summarization automatically extracts information from multiple texts written about the same topic into one summary report. It matters because it lets information consumers quickly familiarize themselves with a large cluster of documents.

tiers.eli5: Imagine many articles about the same news story and one short report that pulls them together. Instead of reading everything, you read the report and get the gist from several sources at once.
tiers.practitioner: These systems complement news aggregators as the next step in coping with information overload. A known difficulty is that it is hard to summarize multiple documents with conflicting views and biases.
tiers.paperLevel: An automatic procedure aimed at extracting information from multiple texts on the same topic, producing a report that is both concise and comprehensive and describes each topic from multiple perspectives. In practice, summarizing documents with conflicting views and biases is hard and nearly impossible in some cases.

explainer.example: A cluster of articles on one topic is condensed into a single report that outlines the topic from multiple perspectives.
